Otto must pick the persona deterministically by keyword matching, not by a classifier call. The pure function `selectPersona(registry, message)` in `apps/api/src/prompt/selectPersona.ts` does this with no I/O. It takes only the registry and the text of the latest customer message. It takes no session, user id or customer number, so the choice is never derived from who the customer is.

The match is a case-insensitive substring match of the message against each persona's `match` keyword list. When several personas match, the first one declared in the registry wins, so the same message always gets the same persona. The choice is made inside the single `beforeModelResponse` hook, through `composePrompt`.

If there is no match, it returns the default persona. It also returns the default, without throwing, for an empty message, a message over 10,000 characters, a missing `defaultPersonaId` (it then returns the first declared persona), or an empty `personas` map (it then returns an empty overlay under the default id).

After selection, `composePrompt` must write the chosen persona's registry `id` to `session.activePersona` on every turn, fallback included.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly describes the pure, deterministic, case-insensitive substring keyword matching with first-declared-wins tie-breaking, but it never says that olt-support is the default persona when nothing matches.
